summary: Spark-only rules protect booking PII/admin keys, validate atomic reservations/cancellations, and restrict public gallery access to encrypted envelopes. Provider-level media privacy and abuse controls remain limited without a backend.

findings.issue: Cloudinary photo URLs remain accessible to their holders; encrypted gallery documents do not revoke media URLs.
findings.recommendation: Treat galleries as password-protected link discovery, not authenticated photo storage. Do not claim expiring/private photo delivery.

findings.issue: Public reservations and public unsigned upload presets do not have trusted per-user/IP rate limits. Encrypted gallery copies can be attacked offline.
findings.recommendation: Use high-entropy gallery passwords, provider-side preset restrictions, and monitor free quotas. Consider authenticated client access if stronger controls become necessary.

findings.issue: Immutable booking receipts and retained Cloudinary assets accumulate.
findings.recommendation: Define retention without re-enabling old cancellation tokens or automatically enabling paid TTL.
